primary_scope.value: Replace 20-year-old Buffalo Forge air handling unit (AHU) serving entire Emergency Department (29,000 SF); renew ER waiting room interior (1,863 SF) including VCT flooring, paint, LED lighting, 2x2 ACT ceiling with insulation, three new interior doors, and new seating furniture. New AHU to serve entire ER with VAV fan operation, economizer controls, hydronic heating/cooling coils, UV lighting, DDC controls integrated to BACnet BAS. Replace hydronic piping, ductwork, and air distribution system for AHU. TAB and commissioning required.
primary_scope.source: RFP SOW §2.1 and BOD General section
primary_scope.quote: The intent of this project is to repair by replacement the AHU servicing the entire Emergency Department (ER), and renew the interior ER waiting room, to include the space's architectural finishes features, along with installing three new interior doors inside ER department within building 2 of Naval Medical Center Portsmouth.

taxonomy_notes.client_type: NMCP is a Navy facility (federal_dod); USACE Huntsville is contracting authority. Also tagged federal_va as NMCP serves veterans, though technically Navy/DoD — primary tag is federal_dod.
taxonomy_notes.program_type: healthcare_military_medical is the best fit for NMCP (DoD MTF). No perfect vocab entry exists for 'Navy Medical Center' vs. 'VA Medical Center' — this is a DoD military treatment facility, not a VA facility.
taxonomy_notes.bfa_role: BFA authored the Basis of Design — indicating they served as the A-E design firm. The RFP is a construction RFP; BFA's A-E role was pre-procurement (design criteria / BOD). Prime_consultant used as best fit. However, it is possible BFA served under NAVFAC or CEHNC as a subconsultant for the BOD work — this is a vocab/spec gap flagged in retro.
taxonomy_notes.delivery_method: This MRR program uses a hybrid model: BFA does the BOD/design criteria, then a MATOC construction contractor provides a 'Work Plan' (essentially design-build of the construction documents) under a firm-fixed-price task order. Closest is design_bid_build (owner's A-E did design, construction contractor builds). MRR programs don't have a perfect delivery_method vocab entry.
taxonomy_notes.award_type: task_order_competition — best value among 4 MATOC holders. Technical approach rated equal to price.
taxonomy_notes.procurement_type: Federal. Competition limited to MATOC restricted pool (4 firms) — this is a 'full and open' competition within the MATOC holders; not a small business set-aside per the documents.

hvac: New Buffalo Forge-equivalent AHU replacing 20-year-old unit serving entire ER (29,000 SF) — VAV fan operation, economizer, hydronic heating/cooling coils, UV lighting, double-wall internally insulated
Variable air volume terminal units (new and rebalanced existing VAVs) with hydronic reheat throughout ER
Complete ductwork replacement in mechanical room; replace louvers and plenum boxes
Replace hydronic distribution piping, valves, strainers, gauges, isolation valves to AHU
ER waiting room: 12 air changes per hour, negative pressurization, 100% exhaust (no return) per UFC 4-510-01
DDC controls replacement (controllers, valves, dampers, sensors) integrated to existing Metasys/BACnet BAS
VFDs on fan motors; NEMA premium efficient motors
TAB (AABC/NEBB/TABB certified firm) and full commissioning by independent CxA
Milk Room option (not exercised): reuse existing VAV box, add diffuser and return grille
electrical: AHU electrical service shutdown and replacement; temporary AHU power via motor control center
ER waiting room: demolition and replacement of lighting fixtures (2x4 LED recessed, LED downlights, LED exit signs, 2x4 LED with battery pack)
Milk Room (option not exercised): new LED 2x4 recessed fixtures, new receptacles and data outlets, salvage motion sensor and card reader
EMT conduit, copper THHN/THWN conductors minimum #12 AWG power / #14 AWG control
Voltage drop: feeders ≤2%, branch circuits ≤3%, overall ≤5%
Lighting levels: Waiting Room 30 FC; Offices/Staff 50 FC per IES/UFC 3-530-01
plumbing: Milk Room option (not exercised only): two new sinks connected to existing water piping
fire_protection: Existing wet pipe sprinkler system (Simplex 4100ES fire alarm; Aurora 481BF fire pump) to remain; temporary protection and reinstatement during ceiling demo
Sprinkler layout reinstatement matching existing manufacturer/type/finish/temperature rating
Milk Room option: sprinkler layout modification per NFPA 13 (Light Hazard for Milk Room, Ordinary Hazard for LDR Supply Room)
Fire alarm smoke detectors and notification appliances: temporary removal and reinstallation at existing locations
LDR Supply Room (Milk Room option): 1-hr fire-rated smoke barrier, 45-minute self-closing door per LSC 18.3.2.1.2

er_waiting_room.demolition: Remove existing ceramic tile and carpet flooring, ceiling tile/grid/insulation (6" batt fiberglass above), three existing doors (one 3' single leaf, two 9' sliding automatic), all wall-mounted items
er_waiting_room.new_work: VCT resilient flooring (approx. 1,863 SF) with 4" resilient base; 5/8" Type X gyp board on 20-ga steel studs 16" OC new partitions; paint (prime + 2 coats); 2x2 ACT ceiling grid with new insulation; one 4070 wood interior door (triage); two trackless automatic aluminum sliding glass doors (corridor/ER waiting); new seating furniture

architectural_scope.milk_technology_room_option_1_not_exerci: Sheet rubber flooring with integral 4" cove base; 2x2 ACT ceiling; new wall partition creating LDR Supply Room; 3070 wood door with HM frame; sliding glass window with SS countertop; copper-infused solid surface countertops, upper cabinets, SS shelves
architectural_scope.gme_building3_option_2_not_exercised: VCT and carpet tile replacement (~1,385 sq yd carpet, 167 sq yd VCT); drywall prep/prime/paint (~22,548 SF); 2,503 LF cove base; 6 phases after hours
architectural_scope.ent_clinic_option_3_not_exercised: Patch/paint (~9,333 SF drywall), wall protection (Acrovyn), 25 doors refinished, sink/casework repair, 2,850 SF ACT ceiling, 1,780 SF VCT, 1,250 LF resilient base; ~9,733 SF total

conflict_flags.resolution_chosen: federal_dod (primary) — Army/USACE is contracting authority, NMCP/Navy is using agency
conflict_flags.rationale: Standard DoD MRR program structure: USACE Huntsville is the construction contracting vehicle for military medical facilities across services. The client relationship is triangular: NMCP (Navy/DoD) is the facility owner; USACE (Army) is the program manager/contracting authority. Both are federal DoD.
